raw_response:
I've farmed this same 1.1 mu in Quzhou for 30 years, wheat then maize, never changed. My husband and son both work off-farm at a factory in the county town, so I'm the one in the field most days, but they come back for the busy times — wheat harvest and maize planting especially, because that window is only a few days and you can't miss it.

With just 1.1 mu, every jin of fertilizer is real money I have to think about. I can't afford to waste, but I also can't afford a bad year — a bad harvest means we don't have enough grain and I have to buy from the market. Last year my wheat gave me about 400 jin per mu, maize about 450 jin. This year I'll do mostly the same.

For wheat, I always buy improved seed from the dealer — I don't save my own anymore, the yield dropped too much. I plant about 15 jin of seed per mu in mid-October. Before planting, I spread 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu — that's the 15-15-15 kind in the white bag, costs about 120 yuan for a 50 kg bag. For my 1.1 mu I need a bit more than one bag for the base dressing. Then in March, when the wheat is turning green and I can see which patches look yellow, I topdress with 50 jin of urea per mu. The extension fellow once told me that's about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, which he said is enough, but my neighbor Auntie Wang uses the same amount and her wheat always looks thicker than mine, so I stick with it. The compound fertilizer also gives me some phosphorus and potassium — I don't fully understand those numbers, but the dealer says the bag has all three, and I've used it for years. I irrigate wheat three times: once after planting if the autumn is dry, once at jointing in late March, and once when the heads come out in April or May. The well water costs electricity, about 15 yuan each time for my small plot, but wheat needs water. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and usually once more for aphids or rust if I see it — so twice for pesticides.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed the same day we finish wheat harvest, sometimes the next morning if we're exhausted. No time to plow deep — I either get my cousin to bring his small rotary tiller for a quick pass, or if he's busy I just hoe rows and plant direct. I put about 30 jin per mu of compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, then at big trumpet stage I spread 40 jin per mu of urea. That's a bit less fertilizer than wheat because maize grows fast in summer when the days are long and hot — it seems to need less pushing. That works out to about 12 kg nitrogen, 2 kg phosphorus, and 2 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once right after planting if the soil is dry, and once when the plants are knee-high. Summer rain helps, but you can't count on it anymore. I spray herbicide once after planting, and if I see corn borer damage on the leaves, I spray insecticide once.

My total spending on fertilizer and seed will be about 400 yuan for the year. If both crops do like last year, I'll get about 900 jin of grain total. I sell what we don't eat — that's maybe 500 jin — and the money goes toward my grandson's school fees. I won't change much from last year. Change is risky when you only have 1.1 mu.
